references.text: The description of a leper as 'unclean' and required to cry this out illustrates the social and religious isolation that leprosy entailed, corresponding to Aaron's comparison with a stillborn child.
Job describes a stillborn child who never saw the light, a parallel to the image of a child born dead from the mother's womb.
Job wishes he had never been born and had gone directly from the mother's womb to the grave, similar to the image of a stillborn child.
Ecclesiastes speaks of a stillborn child as better off than one who lives without enjoying life, a thematic parallel to the image of the stillborn child.
The psalm mentions a stillborn child who never sees the sun, a similar description of premature death from the mother's womb.
